subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm examining the rendered views to spot problems with the gable crown — the gold roof panel reads as a flat slab when seen edge-on from the side, suggesting the extrude thickness for the gold and navy layers needs reworking.

Looking further, the side panel of the case looks too plain and flat, with grain texture but no inset detail, so I'm thinking about adding a gilt panel or rune carving there to match the front vines. I'm also checking the alignment of the front posts and case front to make sure the post radius and z-position don't clip through the case geometry.

Checking through the internal structure now — shelves, books, and the starry back panel all seem positioned correctly relative to the dais and bay heights, though the back of the case is just a plain navy slab since it's never seen. The orb resting on the books in bay 1 looks fine but I want to double check it doesn't overlap awkwardly in the front view.

For the candelabra, the basket currently hides its base behind it, so I should reposition the basket slightly to avoid that overlap. The scroll inside the basket looks fine as is, and the ground shadow oddity isn't something I introduced. Now I'm placing the floor scrolls at their z-positions.

I'm checking the candelabra and basket placement relative to the rune ring to avoid overlap, deciding to keep the rune at 1.1 and nudge the basket aside. For the floating motes, I notice some look like thin lines when viewed from the side since they're flat extrusions seen edge-on, so I'm fixing this by adding a second extrude rotated 90° (or using an octahedron shape) to give them volume from any angle.

Now I'm thinking the dais looks a bit flat and needs more visual interest, so I'm planning to add glowing crystal clusters at the back corners using octahedron or cone shapes to give it some sparkle and depth.

The gold gable roof reads too noisy and mottled right now, so I'm reconsidering the metal paint settings — maybe toning down the tarnish/size for a calmer, richer gold rather than the dirty-looking patch it currently has.

The purple wood grain also looks too blotchy and carpet-like, so I'm thinking about adjusting the noise size and considering swapping to a stripe-based plank pattern instead for a cleaner wood look.

Next, the side view of the case looks too blank, so I'm planning to add a gilt inset frame with a glowing rune or emblem on both outer side faces near the post edges.

Still working out panel positions...

Settling on frame 0.32, panel 0.28, emblem 0.2. For the emblem plane I'm rotating it 90° around y so it faces outward on each side, mirroring for the opposite side with -90°, positioning it on the CASE parent with a gold glow. I'll skip adding extra detail to the gabled crown and move on to checking the front view.

Checking the scrolls and levitating book placement, the armillary sphere, and floating motes -- all look fine. For the wizard theme I'm considering adding a pointy wizard hat somewhere on top of the case, built from a lathe brim and cone shape in navy with a gold band and star decal, positioned in the open space near the armillary.

But there's not much clearance since the gable spans wide and the armillary and candle stacks occupy the flanks, so I'm reconsidering where the hat could actually fit without overlapping existing pieces.

I'll place it standing on the floor near the front-left, built as a lathed cone profile with a flared brim and slightly curved tip for charm, plus a thin gold torus band around the base and a simple star accent on the front.

Let me double-check positions against nearby objects: the hat's footprint overlaps slightly with the scroll and the stack, so I'll nudge the hat to around x=-0.6, z=0.7 to keep clearances clean.

Now I'm working out the crystal cluster placement — a few tilted cone shapes with a glow effect, positioned symmetrically on either side with one main taller crystal.

I'm checking the basket placement against the rune circle, dais edge, and candelabra to avoid overlaps — settling on bx 0.75, bz 0.7 keeps it within the dais boundary and clear of the candelabra's base radius.

Since the basket could occlude the candelabra in the front view, I'm repositioning the candelabra to x 1.08, z 0.05, verifying its base radius stays within the dais edge and keeps enough screen separation from the basket (0.5–0.9 vs 0.91–1.19). Now moving on to placing the book stack on the left mirror side.

I'm locating the unique variable declarations for the candelabra and basket coordinates so I can edit each one individually without ambiguity, then planning to replace the mote loop with two separate extrude calls.

I'm cleaning up a stray `b.cylinderPlaceholder?.()` line that isn't needed, then adding the new additions right before the `return b.root;` statement, checking that search text is unique. I'll skip adding extra rune rings or gilt ridge details and move on to the hat's lathe geometry.

Working out the hat band and star placement, calculating torus radius along the hat profile curve at different heights to position the gilt band and star accent correctly.

Now I'm writing a helper to generate crystal clusters using scaled octahedron geometries, computing the vertical scale factor from height and radius, then placing a tilted cluster of cyan and pink crystals near the base.

Checking the placement math — rotation happens around the translated base so tilts work correctly, and I need to verify the crystals sit on the right dais step by checking their radial distance against the step radii, adjusting positions like (±1.0, -0.65) so they land properly instead of floating.
